[CHANNEL: ARJUN] Why does QLoRA NF4 + gradient checkpointing let a 7B model train inside 8 GB VRAM?

Three memory wins combine: 1) NF4 quantizes frozen 7B base weights from ~14 GB FP16 down to ~4.5 GB. 2) LoRA updates only small low-rank matrices (`r=16`, <1% params). 3) Gradient checkpointing + `paged_adamw_8bit` trade minor compute to keep activation spikes inside 8 GB VRAM.

1) Computing a subsampled CRC32 hash of pixels + quantized cursor position skips static frames in microseconds, preventing Wi-Fi decode queues. 2) Compositing the exact Win32 cursor directly onto the frame guarantees the mobile canvas shows true click alignment regardless of Windows hardware cursor hiding.
